problem:
A triangle $D$ has vertices $(0,0),(-1,0),(0,-1).$  What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

feedback.problem:
The unit square $D$ has vertices $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}0 & -9 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

$\text{Area}(T(D))=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095768/assets/6805467a24cb40559f205cbfcecc4f5a34ff2ec6ebda8ae67f997c02f123b53c.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=1\cdot 1=1.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=0\cdot 1-(-9)\cdot 4=36.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,36\,|\cdot 1 \\  & =36.\end{aligned}
$$
